fields.v: Dillon, D., Varanasi, K. (2026). Context-Augmented Code Generation: How Product Context Improves AI Coding Agent Decision Compliance by 49%. arXiv:2605.08112v1 [cs.SE], 27 Apr 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2605.08112v1, marked 'Preprint'; no published venue
Brief (briefhq.ai), the company that makes the Brief product evaluated (both authors)

Compares; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — Claude Code baseline vs Claude Code + Brief on a controlled benchmark; introduces the decision-compliance benchmark dcbench (8 tasks, 41 weighted decision points)
fields.why: Judgement: Brief is the authors' own product and its workflow (spec generation, mid-build consultation) is described, so a reader could file the study as 'Proposes an approach' (then Q13 applies); the paper presents its contribution as the benchmark and the comparison (abstract, p. 1-2), not Brief itself
fields.doubt: A Brief é produto dos autores e o fluxo é descrito, mas o artigo apresenta como contributo o benchmark e a comparação. Decide se a natureza inclui 'Proposes an approach' (então a Q13 aplica-se).

Automatic: regex pass/fail checks on git diffs, API usage logs for cost/tokens/turns, lint/typecheck/test runs; LLM-as-judge (Claude Sonnet, 5 rubrics). Manual: one blind reviewer checked the 16 PR pairs against the same criteria (within ±5% of automated) and judged merge-readiness

Criteria stated by the authors: weighted decision compliance (regex + human check) and merge-readiness (binary human judgement: would merge as-is vs requires rework); no cost criterion stated. Averages over 3 runs. -- Claude Code baseline (claude -p, 5-min timeout) + Claude Sonnet 4.6 coding (Opus 4.6 planning per p. 4/12, see Notes): compliance 19/41 (46%); 2/8 tasks at 100%, 2/8 at 0%; 5 blocking violations; merge-ready 2/8; tests written 0; build pass lint/typecheck 100%, tests 0%; total cost $4.13, 3,902K tokens, 165 turns, ~5.1 min/task; per-task cost $0.13-0.67 where reported; cost per merge-ready task $2.07; cost per correct decision $0.22. Quality: does not work (merge-ready on 2/8 tasks; authors: its runs 'predominantly produce output that requires human rework'); cost: no criterion stated by the authors. Baseline. -- Claude Code + Brief (brief build --confirm, 30-min timeout) + Opus 4.6 planning / Sonnet 4.6 coding: compliance 39/41 (95%); 6/8 tasks at 100%, 0 at 0%; 0 blocking violations; merge-ready 8/8; 838 tests; build pass 100% all; total cost $5.28, 3,867K tokens, 187 turns, ~15 min/task; per-task cost $0.55-0.82 where reported; cost per merge-ready task $0.66; cost per correct decision $0.14. Quality: works (merge-ready on 8/8 tasks); cost: no criterion stated by the authors. Config C (external orchestrator) not reported
fields.why: Both cost verdicts ('partly' for the baseline, 'works' for CC + Brief) rested on thresholds set by the extractor; the authors state no cost criterion, so replaced by 'no criterion stated by the authors' (rule of 2026-11-23). Quality verdicts now cite the authors' merge-readiness criterion; 'does not work' for 2/8 merge-ready is a reading of that criterion. Added baseline per-task costs (p. 7-11)

fields.v: Project: one seeded repository (dcbench), 8 tasks designed by the authors with 15 seeded decisions. Configurations: Claude Code vs Claude Code + Brief. Baseline: Claude Code with codebase only, no spec. Held constant: models (Opus 4.6 planning, Sonnet 4.6 coding), identical prompts without hints, repository; differences: timeout (5 vs 30 min), workflow (spec + mid-build consultation) and context. Acceptance tests: regex pass/fail checks per decision, human blind review; no functional test suite for tasks. Repetitions: 3 independent runs per task and configuration (48 runs). Human intervention: none during runs stated

Claude Code + Brief better on compliance by 49 points (95% vs 46%), largest gap on decisions invisible in code (baseline 0-33%, Brief 100%); zero gap on code-visible tasks TASK-012/013. Merge-ready 8/8 vs 2/8. Total cost +28%, tokens -1%, duration ~3x; cost per merge-ready task -68%, per correct decision -36%. SD across runs ≤0.5 decision points per task; no significance tests

Distinguished the two configurations clearly; 3 runs with low SD. Limitations stated: benchmark designed by the authors to create a gap (best case for context augmentation), partially circular (scores the same decisions Brief retrieves), no stronger baselines (spec-only, context-only, manual criteria), one confounded comparison (context + spec workflow + consultation), single human reviewer, one repository and one model family

Proof-of-concept, directional evidence only; confound of context retrieval vs structured spec workflow not isolated; needs ablations (codebase + spec only, codebase + context only, manual acceptance criteria), multiple reviewers, more repositories, languages and model families; Brief-specific implementation

Vendor study (authors from Brief). Title and abstract '49%' are percentage points. Model use for the baseline unclear: p. 4 says Sonnet 4.6 handles all code generation with no spec, while p. 4/12 say Opus 4.6 drives planning 'in both configurations'. Timeouts differ (5 vs 30 min). Table 3 gives CC + Brief TASK-004 3/4 (75%) while Table 10 shows both decisions PASS, and p. 6 says the augmented configuration achieves 100% 'across the board' (Table 5) despite 5/6 and 3/4 in Table 3. TASK-001 CC + Brief: p. 8 says only one of three runs lost credit (2 of 3 weight points on D-002), which averages to 5.67/6, yet the score is given as 5/6. Abstract (p. 1) says the baseline achieves 100% on decisions visible in the codebase, but Table 5 marks D-004 (50%), D-009 (0%) and D-013 (0%) as visible in code ('Yes', 'Yes (skipped)', 'Yes (missed)'); the text on p. 6 lists only the visible decisions at 100%. Table 2 'Avg Merge-Ready' delta '+75%' is a difference in points (25% to 100%). Tables 2-4 jumbled by pdftotext; values rebuilt from text p. 5-6. LLM-as-judge rubric scores not reported. Benchmark repository, 16 PRs and harness released (github.com/brief-hq/dcbench). No pre-registration. Programming language: TypeScript
fields.why: Incomplete: added the contradiction between the abstract's claim (100% on code-visible decisions) and Table 5, where three decisions marked visible score 0-50% for the baseline

Partly (0.5): main result follows and the confound is acknowledged, but title and 'driven by product context' framing over-attribute; inconsistencies between Tables 3, 5 and 10
fields.why: Judgement: the discussion and conclusion hedge carefully (directional evidence, confound stated), so a reader could give Yes; the title, the 'driven by product context' framing and the reported-score inconsistencies (Tables 3, 5, 10; abstract vs Table 5 on visible decisions) support Partly
fields.doubt: As conclusões são cautelosas e o confound é admitido, mas o título atribui o ganho ao contexto e há inconsistências entre o resumo e as Tabelas 3, 5 e 10. Decide entre Partly e Yes.
